[[2019–20 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten regular season]] co-champions | tourney = | tourney_result = }} {{2019–20 Big Ten men's basketball standings}} The '''2019–20 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by ninth-year head coach [[Mark Turgeon]] and played their home games at [[Xfinity Center (College Park, Maryland)|Xfinity Center]] in [[College Park, Maryland]], as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. With a win over [[2019–20 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] on March 8, 2020, the Terrapins earned a share of their first-ever Big Ten regular season championship. They finished the season 24–7, 14–6 in [[2019–20 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a three-way tie for first place. Their season ended following the cancellation of postseason tournaments due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2020-ncaa-tournament-canceled-due-to-growing-threat-of-coronavirus-pandemic/|title=2020 NCAA Tournament canceled due to growing threat of coronavirus pandemic|website=CBSSports.com|language=en|access-date=2020-03-16}} ==Previous season== The [[2018–19 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Terrapins]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] 23–11, 13–7 in [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in fifth place. They lost in the second round of the [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] to [[2018–19 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 6 seed in the East region. There they defeated [[2018–19 Belmont Bruins men's basketball team|Belmont]] before losing to [[2018–19 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]] in the second round. ==Offseason== ===Coaching changes=== In May 2019, assistant [[Kevin Broadus]] was hired as the new head coach at [[Morgan State Bears men's basketball|Morgan State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.coachesdatabase.com/kevin-broadus-hired-morgan-state/|title=Morgan State officially hires Kevin Broadus as head coach|website=coachesdatabase.com|publisher=Coaches Database|date=May 2, 2019|accessdate=November 4, 2019}} Turgeon hired DeAndre Haynes as Broadus' replacement in June 2019.{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/06/07/maryland-basketball-expected-hire-former-michigan-assistant-deandre-haynes/|title=Maryland basketball hires former Michigan assistant DeAndre Haynes|work=Washington Post|date=June 10, 2019|accessdate=November 4, 2019}} ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
